name: Women's Class B blue long-sleeve blouse, tie tab and skirt (nametag position only)
size_basis: Silhouette (long sleeves, collar, torso, trousers/skirt) measured from CAPR 39-1 Figure 4.11 (3 March 2020): the figure was rendered at 2.2x, traced, and scaled with the registration of its short-sleeve twin to the short-sleeve base image, so interior parts line up with garment-blues-class-b-blouse-female. No real garment was measured. Then the whole sheet is scaled by 1.2171 (LIVE-ART2 item 1; 0.0385 in/px becomes 0.0469): the men's pocket measures 4.31 in wide on the traced image, and a USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt pocket is about 5.25 in wide x 6 in tall (ESTIMATE: AF shirt pattern dimension supplied with the task, no CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903 dimension; the CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.9 nametag (3 3/8 in) read as a ruler gives a smaller 4.56 in, the figure is schematic), so K = 5.25 / 4.313. The blouse has no pocket: it keeps its registration to the men's sleeve-to-sleeve width and takes the same K (button pitch 4.3 in; Fig 4.10 read with the nametag as a ruler gives 4.0). Nameplate, epaulet strap width, buttons and strokes stay true size.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box; sleeve_flat_view {left:{x,y},right:{x,y}} is where the top_center of the flat sleeve assets <id>-sleeve-flat-left / -right sits beside the figure (outboard of each arm, its top at the shoulder seam height, 1 in clear of the sleeve outline; it lies outside this artwork box)

epaulet_strap.edge_on: LIVE10-ART 2: drawn edge-on like the Class A board strip: a band edge_thickness_in thick, its upper edge the shoulder line, its outer end the armhole seam, the point and the button foreshortened across it; width_in is the strap's TRUE width (the top view's)

measured.figure: CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.10 (women's short-sleeve figure, first blouse), the 3 3/8 in nametag as ruler read x 1.075 to this sheet's scale (41.3 px/in)

epaulet_strap.note: the strap lies along the shoulder line N-SP of the finished silhouette (dimensions.finishing), its upper edge IS that line, its outer end is the armhole seam, a band 0.46 in thick (LIVE10-ART 2; the true strap is 1.0 in wide as commit 72a36ce9); the button 1/2 in from the tip is the brief's value, no figure shows it under the sleeve; the sheet's whole shoulder line is 5.53 in

tie.source: LIVE9-ART 1: the Class A women's coat sheet's own tab (make-blues-a-female.js, tie.js): dx 2.503, dy 2.808, ex 0.240, ey 0.927, t 1.000 in, apex at the collar junction J, the arms cut under the leaf points on a slanted line as the Class A's are cut by the coat's V edge (CAPR 39-1 4.1.12.4, Figs 4.7a, 4.11)

collar.source: LIVE9-ART 1: the two leaves close on the knot at the junction J (the lowest point of the neck opening, the long-sleeve outline's neck bowl on all four sheets); each leaf is top end, shoulder vertex, collar point, junction and the neck-opening vertices back up; the leading edge J to P is 3.07 in long (points about 3 in; Fig 4.8 measured 3.9 in at 48 px/in on the figure's own pocket scale, the Class A coat leaf 2.65 in); direction 50 deg from vertical (Class A coat leaf edge 37 to 40 deg men, 50 deg women; Fig 4.8 30 deg). No regulation dimension.

finishing.note: shoulder line straightened between the neck vertex and the shoulder point, armhole seam from the shoulder point to the armpit apex, hem hook / gap bulge removed (finishShoulderArmpit)

scale.note: pocket 5.25 x 6 in = USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt (estimate); the whole sheet scaled so the traced pocket width equals it

sleeve_widening.note: outward warp of the sleeve between the armhole seam and the outer edge (seam, body, shoulder and straps unmoved) so the true-size 3 1/2 in chevron lies between the outline and the armhole seam; an estimate, the regulation gives no sleeve width
sleeve_widening.chevron_fit_note: clearance in inches from every row of the 3 1/2 in chevron, placed as the engine does (visual centre on chevron_halfway, turned along shoulder_seam to elbow), to the outer edge and to the armhole seam; positive = on the sleeve. The women's 4 in option (4.1.12.2.3.3, the 3 1/2 in art scaled to 4.00 x 6.54 in) is listed under 4 and still overhangs, clipped to the silhouette by the engine

documented: long-sleeve blouse with rounded cuffs and buttonhole closures, epaulets, no military creases (CAPR 39-1 4.1.9.5 / 4.1.12.2)
blue satin tie tab with the long-sleeve blouse (4.1.12)
nameplate centred on the wearer's right, even with to 1.5 in above/below the first exposed button (4.1.12.2.4.1)
assumed: px-to-inch scale (women's base image drawn larger on its canvas; rescaled to match the men's shirt width, then x K like the men's shirt)
nameplate size (3.375 x 0.75 in = Vanguard CAP0599M cadet name plate (blue plastic, 3 3/8 x 3/4 in); no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903; no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903)

epaulet strap drawn on the sheet from the shoulder line, edge-on: a band 0.46 in thick (the true strap is 1.0 in wide), 0.5 in point, button 1/2 in from the tip (the brief's value) foreshortened across the band, one line of topstitch 0.09 in in (dimensions.epaulet_strap)
pocket and seam geometry read off the base image
collar leaves: the Class A coat's closed collar construction, leading edge about 3 in, an estimate (dimensions.collar)
shirt, trouser/skirt and line colours sampled from the base image
sleeve widening: the sleeve is drawn wider than the traced hanging view (CFG.widen, dimensions.sleeve_widening)
belt strap colour #14347f (and its #7d95d6 stitching) is a choice, not sampled: the base image paints the belt the same navy as the trousers; regulation says only blue belt (4.1.11.1.1.5, 4.1.12.7)
skirt cut off at the base image's crop line
